answer: Empires of standing are fraud's dream: one name holding influence across every domain at once. Cap territory instead. Any identity may hold deep standing along one ridge of work - a few adjacent domains - but spread collapses multiplicatively: domain N+1 costs exponentially more than N. A sparrow holds a hedgerow, not a continent, and the hedgerow is defensible. Clones exist to bridge domains cheaply; make bridging the expensive thing. Dunes migrate: identities may relocate their ridge, trading old for new domain standing at a market-set rate - movement possible, never free.
